summary: A description of how to use Harvard's PDP-10 program for network remote job entry, which at that time worked only with UCLA. A user starts the program, opens a Telnet connection to UCLA for commands, and uses FTP-style commands to submit jobs and get results.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how to use Harvard's RJE program to submit work to UCLA's Remote Job Service. It covers local commands, UCLA commands, and retrieving results.

questions: submitting jobs to ucla over arpanet
subtitle: A guide to Harvard's remote job entry program for UCLA's RJS.

tldr.problem: Users needed instructions for submitting jobs to UCLA's Remote Job Service from Harvard's PDP-10.
tldr.mechanism: Harvard's RJE program connects to UCLA, sends job input, and retrieves print and punch output using local and remote commands.
tldr.outcome: The RFC explains a service that was implemented for UCLA and lists its account, command, and output-handling requirements.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 499's status as Unknown. The RFC is a user guide for Harvard's RJE program and its UCLA installation.

sections.title: Harvard's Network RJE
sections.content: Harvard's Remote Job Entry program was designed to let network users submit jobs to remote servers and retrieve results using Harvard's PDP-10. At the time described, the program was implemented for UCLA, and users needed an account and password arranged at UCLA.
sections.plainLanguage: Harvard's program let users send jobs to UCLA and retrieve their results. The guide says the described installation worked with UCLA.

sections.title: Local and UCLA Commands
sections.content:
The program opens a TELNET connection to UCLA for commands and error messages. Harvard commands begin with an asterisk: READ sends a file of job cards, JCL, program, and data; PRINT retrieves output and formats it for a PDP-10 line printer; QUIT closes the connections.

Other commands are sent to UCLA's Remote Job Service. The RFC distinguishes these local and remote command processors.
sections.plainLanguage: Commands beginning with an asterisk control Harvard's program. Other commands go to UCLA's job service.

sections.title: Queues and Retrieving Output
sections.content:
UCLA's RJS directs output to an Active or Deferred queue. Opening the print or punch channel sends output from the Active Queue; output in the Deferred Queue must be requested by job name using RESET.

The guide describes commands to change the default destination or deferral status, route output, cancel jobs, restart output, and request additional copies.
sections.plainLanguage: Some output is sent when a channel opens; deferred output must be requested by job name. Other commands manage jobs and where their output goes.
